subject: Dedicated GPU capacity: mapping memory vs latency outcomes for Anvil Labs procurement
messages:
From: Samantha Reyes <samantha@anvillabs.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Li <marco.li@anvillabs.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing call follow-up - memory/latency constraints

Thanks for the call this morning, Vivek. Quick recap from our side: Anvil's inference surface is heavily multimodal (short text prompts + image tokens) and we have several endpoints that must stay below 50ms p95. Our initial usage profile (pilot) expects a steady 250 reqs/minute with occasional bursts to 800 rpm.

Question for Redwood: which Dedicated SKU would give us the best chance to meet the 50ms p95 while holding monthly cost within our cap? We assume model is a trimmed 20B with 48k context; memory overhead per model is a concern. Also curious about cold-start behavior for L4 instances vs H100.

Samantha
Head of Engineering, Anvil Labs

---

Note: attaching procurement email separately to include contract timeline.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reyes <samantha@anvillabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sizing call follow-up - memory/latency constraints

Thanks Samantha — great context. I pulled together a short comparison and a suggested starting configuration; attaching a one-pager and the microbenchmark summary. High level guidance below so procurement can see tradeoffs quickly:

Summary (short):
- H100 (80GB)
  - Pros: best headroom for large KV caches / long contexts; typically lowest p95 for heavy-attention models; more resilient under bursty tails.
  - Cons: highest unit cost; over-provisioning risk if peak bursts are rare.
- A100 (40GB vRAM)
  - Pros: solid middle ground for throughput-focused workloads; lower cost than H100 and more predictable latency for steady throughput.
  - Cons: may require more instance parallelism and sharding for 48k context models; KV cache pressure can increase effective tail latency.
- L4 (24GB)
  - Pros: cheapest per-slot and excellent for short-context, dense-batching scenarios; fast cold-starts for lightweight variants.
  - Cons: limited memory for long contexts and larger KV caches; higher risk of latency spikes as batch sizes and cache misses increase.

Recommendation (pilot stage):
- Start with a small pool: 6x A100 slots + 2x H100 dedicated for KV-heavy endpoints. The A100s handle steady throughput; H100s absorb peaks and long-context requests.
- Configure per-endpoint routing: latency-sensitive endpoints route to H100 first, fallback to A100, and only route to L4 for non-critical batch workloads.
- Enable prefix caching and a warm-kept hotset on H100s (we can automate warmers) to limit cold-start exposure for long-context calls.

Next steps:
- Ben/LA to share a brief ops playbook and cost estimate (I included a conservative cost delta in the attached PDF).
- Samantha: confirm pilot duration and preferred SLA window so we can size required reserved slots vs burst.

Vivek
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: internal sizing notes / cost delta (Anvil pilot)

Vivek / Lauren — forwarding the quick ops note I drafted after the benchmarking run. Key numbers below (summarized):

Benchmarks (representative):
- 20B trimmed model (48k context), token-gen heavy:
  - H100 @ 80GB: median latency 22ms, p95 38ms, tokens/sec per slot 540
  - A100 @ 40GB: median 30ms, p95 62ms, tokens/sec per slot 420
  - L4 @ 24GB: median 44ms, p95 120ms, tokens/sec per slot 260

Memory considerations:
- Effective KV cache sizing for 48k context pushes A100 to ~70% usable memory for model + cache; H100 gives ~30% extra headroom for larger hotsets. L4 cannot hold the large hotset, so it must rely on more frequent remote cache fetches (higher tail risk).

Operational playbook highlights:
- Warm pools: keep at least one hot H100 warm per critical endpoint to guarantee cold-start latency budget.
- Autoscale policy: aggressive tail-based scaling on A100s, conservative on H100s (to avoid cost churn).
- Fallback policy: circuit-breaker from H100 -> A100 -> L4 for non-critical traffic; instant failover to smaller quantized variants for cost-sensitive requests.

Cost delta (monthly, estimated pilot):
- Pilot (6 A100 + 2 H100 + optional 4 L4 for batch): ~ $72k/mo (reserved discounts included).
- All-H100 approach (8 H100): ~ $180k/mo.

Note: I attached the spreadsheet with per-instance assumptions and burst cost model. If they want to lower cost, we can: reduce H100 count and rely on smart routing, or quantize the model which reduces memory and increases throughput on A100/L4.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final sizing note + recommended pilot plan (attached)

Samantha / Marco / Procurement team — linking the attachments and the mutual action plan for your procurement review. Below is the concrete pilot proposal we discussed, written as an MPO (mutual pilot outline) so procurement can slot dates: 

Pilot outline (6 weeks):
- Reserved: 6x A100 (primary pool) + 1x H100 (hot reserve) for the first 4 weeks.
- Burst: enable up to 2x burst H100 for scheduled demo windows (manual button for first month).
- Optional: 2x L4 for nightly batch jobs (ingest/embedding pipeline).
- Observability: enable token-level cost and p95 tracing on all endpoints; Redwood will run a weekly review and a regression check against the sample prompt set.

Why this reduces risk:
- Keeps steady throughput on A100s (cost-effective) while guaranteeing a warm hotset on H100 for strict 50ms p95 endpoints.
- Limits H100 spend by using it as a reserved hot cache rather than the primary workhorse.
- L4s are used only when memory pressure is low or for non-latency-critical batch work.

Ask from Anvil:
- Confirm pilot start date window (we proposed Mar 28 — Apr 8).
- Sign and return the attached MAP and procurement quote by Mar 22 to lock reserved pricing.

If you want, we can also run a small 48-hour controlled A/B where identical traffic splits between (A) A100-only pool and (B) A100 + H100 hot reserve so you can see p95 improvements empirically.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to finalize timelines.

Vivek Kulkarni
